items.title: Bulk abstract ingest robot
items.text: This robot improves abstract coverage in the DESTinY Open Search index by taking large result sets exported from academic databases (currently Scopus via the Academic API Importer) and offering their abstracts as enhancements to references that are missing one — or whose current abstract looks broken.

items.title: What it does
items.text:
• Ingests JSONL exports from Azure blob storage into a local Postgres metadata cache, with checkpoints so a crashed transfer can resume where it left off.
  • Matches cached records against the DESTinY repository by identifier (OpenAlex ID or DOI by default) and checks that the match is plausible (publication year, title similarity).
  • Submits an AbstractContentEnhancement plus a RawEnhancement (the untouched source metadata) for every reference that passes the enhancement rules.

items.title: What it deliberately does not do
items.text:
This is a temporary measure to improve coverage until the proper, full-fledged ingestion flow with deduplication and (partial) data fusion is in place. Accordingly, there are intentional decisions:

  • no full deduplication — records are matched by a single identifier only, the DOI unless MATCH_IDENTIFIER says otherwise,
  • no creating new references (canonicals) in the index — existing references are only enhanced,
  • no heavy transformation — raw source data is stored as-is and parsed lazily, with a thin per-format parser; a payload it cannot parse is parked with encountered_parsing_error rather than breaking the flow,
  • no data fusion — new metadata is not merged and existing values are not replaces by picking the "better" one.

Temporary project

This robot is meant to be deprecated once a complete ingestion pipeline with proper deduplication exists. Changes should be weighed against that end goal (see the discussion in issue #7).

items.title: The flow at a glance
items.text:
Three small runner processes work through the pipeline, communicating only via the Postgres database and the repository:

flowchart TD
    subgraph source["Source"]
        API["Academic API Importer"]
        BLOB[("Azure blob<br/>storage<br/><i>JSONL export</i>")]
    end

    subgraph ods["DESTinY repository"]
        REPO["References &<br/>enhancement batches"]
    end

    subgraph cache["Metadata cache (Postgres)"]
        INGEST[("search_ingest<br/><i>transfer requests</i>")]
        RECORDS[("records<br/><i>raw records +<br/>tracking state</i>")]
        MATCHES[("m2m_record_ods<br/><i>record ↔ reference<br/>pairs + flags</i>")]
    end

    subgraph robot["Bulk abstract ingest robot"]
        QUEUE["Queue runner<br/><code>queue.py</code>"]
        MATCH["Match runner<br/><code>match.py</code>"]
        ENHANCE["Enhance runner<br/><code>enhance.py</code>"]
    end

    API -->|"upload result file"| BLOB
    BLOB -->|"stream JSONL"| QUEUE
    INGEST -.->|"transfer request<br/>(SAS link)"| QUEUE
    QUEUE -->|"store raw records"| RECORDS
    RECORDS -->|"unevaluated batch"| MATCH
    MATCH -->|"one row per matched<br/>reference"| MATCHES
    MATCHES -->|"records to enhance<br/>(by DESTinY ID)"| ENHANCE
    RECORDS -->|"raw payload"| ENHANCE
    %% MATCH -->|"log eligibility"| RECORDS
    MATCH -->|"lookup by configured<br/>identifier (DOI),<br/>request enhancements"| REPO
    REPO -->|"approved batches"| ENHANCE
    ENHANCE -->|"submit abstract +<br/>raw enhancements"| REPO

Each runner runs its own endless loop and can be restarted at any time — all progress is tracked in the database. The individual steps are explained in Architecture.

items.title: Where to go next
items.text:
• Architecture — the three runners, how they hand work to each other, and how the design survives crashes.
  • Data model — the three tables (search_ingest, records, m2m_record_ods) and their tracking columns.
  • Enhancement rules — when an abstract is considered worth submitting, including the decision tree.
  • Configuration — all environment variables and logging options.
  • Monitoring — how progress is tracked in the database, compacted, and viewed.
  • Development & operations — setting up a dev environment, running the robot, Docker Compose, deployment notes.

items.title: Project structure
items.text:
run_robot.py            # Typer CLI entry point (tasks: match, enhance, queue)
app/
├── robots/             # The runners — one loop task per module
│   ├── queue.py        #   blob storage → records table ("transfer")
│   ├── match.py        #   records → repository lookups + enhancement requests
│   └── enhance.py      #   approved batches → enhancement submissions
├── util/               # Shared runner boilerplate
│   ├── runner.py       #   Abstract Runner base class (main loop, shutdown)
│   ├── repository.py   #   DESTinY repository client wrapper
│   ├── config.py       #   pydantic-settings (env vars / .env)
│   └── logging.py      #   logging config loader
└── db/                 # Models and database wrapper
    ├── schemas.py      #   SQLModel models (Record, SearchIngest, …)
    ├── engine.py       #   async engine/session helpers
    ├── store.py        #   AbstractStore — queries for match/enhance runners
    └── ingest.py       #   IngestTracker — transfer requests, checkpoints, locks
scripts/                # Ops SQL — metrics tracking, compaction, ad-hoc monitoring

Both tables are created automatically by SQLModel on startup, so a plain Postgres instance (or the postgres service in compose.yaml) is all that's needed.

items.title: Architecture
items.text: The robot is a set of small, independent runner processes that never talk to each other directly. They coordinate exclusively through the Postgres metadata cache and the DESTinY repository itself. Every runner is a Runner subclass (app/util/runner.py) executing one _loop_task() repeatedly, with a configurable pause between iterations for graceful API use.

items.title: Runners
items.text: Runner Module Loop interval Job Queue runner app/robots/queue.py QUEUE_INTERVAL_SECONDS (default 1 h) Streams JSONL files from Azure blob storage into the records table, checkpointing progress on the search_ingest row. Match runner app/robots/match.py MATCH_INTERVAL_SECONDS (default 30 s) Takes a batch of not-yet-evaluated records, looks them up in the repository by the identifier configured in MATCH_IDENTIFIER (DOI by default), filters them through the enhancement rules and requests enhancements. Enhance runner app/robots/enhance.py ENHANCE_INTERVAL_SECONDS (default 30 s) Polls the repository for approved enhancement batches, fetches the abstracts from the cache and submits the enhancements.

items.title: End-to-end sequence
items.text:
sequenceDiagram
    autonumber
    participant API as Academic API Importer
    participant Blob as Azure blob storage
    participant DB as Postgres cache
    participant Q as Queue runner
    participant M as Match runner
    participant ODS as DESTinY repository
    participant E as Enhance runner

    API->>Blob: upload JSONL result file
    API->>DB: insert search_ingest row (SAS link)
    loop every QUEUE_INTERVAL_SECONDS
        Q->>DB: claim open transfer request (file lock, mark queueing)
        Q->>Blob: stream file from checkpoint offset
        Q->>DB: insert raw records (batched, with checkpoints)
        Q->>DB: mark request queued
    end
    loop every MATCH_INTERVAL_SECONDS
        M->>DB: take next request batch (unevaluated records)
        M->>ODS: lookup references by MATCH_IDENTIFIER (DOI by default)
        M->>M: apply enhancement rules
        M->>ODS: POST /enhancement-requests/ for eligible references
        M->>DB: persist all tracking flags atomically
    end
    Note over ODS: repository approves / schedules batches
    loop every ENHANCE_INTERVAL_SECONDS
        E->>ODS: poll next enhancement batch
        ODS-->>E: batch info + blob URL with reference JSONL
        E->>DB: load cache entries for the batch's DESTinY IDs
        E->>Blob: upload enhancements JSONL (abstract + raw)
        E->>ODS: finalise batch result
        E->>DB: mark matches as submitted
    end

items.title: The match → enhance handoff
items.text:
The match and enhance runners never share in-memory state. For every reference it matched, the match runner writes a m2m_record_ods row (the reference's destiny_id plus the abstract_enhancement_required and enhancement_requested flags for that pair); the enhance runner later re-reads the cache entries by DESTinY ID — through that table — when the repository hands out an approved batch. This means:

  • the repository decides when work is done (the robot only polls),
  • the robot can restart at any point without losing track of what was requested vs. submitted,
  • the data actually submitted is re-fetched from the cache at submission time, so it always matches the latest parsed state of the record.

items.title: Sharing work between processes
items.text:
Two mechanisms allow multiple worker processes to run without double work:

Row-level locks in deterministic order. When the match runner persists its tracking flags, it first acquires SELECT … FOR UPDATE row locks sorted by record_id. Workers touching overlapping batches serialise cleanly instead of deadlocking (see AbstractStore.persist_match_results).

File locks per transfer. Each search_ingest transfer is guarded by an OS-level file lock (AsyncFileLock under TRANSFER_LOCKS_PATH) keyed by the ingest ID, so several queue-runner processes on one host can compete for work without transferring the same file twice. A runner takes the first request it can lock and processes it exclusively.

items.title: Crash resilience
items.text:
Failure Recovery Queue runner dies mid-file Progress was checkpointed (checkpoint_bytes / checkpoint_rows) at every API_WRAPPER_CHECKPOINT_INTERVAL rows; the next run resumes streaming at that byte offset. Match runner dies mid-batch All provenance writes happen in one atomic transaction — either every tracking flag for the batch is written, or none. Records are re-processed on the next poll. Enhance runner dies before finalising a batch The repository never sees a completed batch result and will hand it out again. Double-submitting enhancements is acceptable by design. A single record cannot be parsed The match runner logs a warning and flags the row encountered_parsing_error; the rest of the batch is processed normally. The row stays parked until the flag is reset after a parser fix (see Data model → Parser fixes). Whole host dies File locks are released by the OS; checkpoints and tracking flags in Postgres tell the next run exactly where to continue.

A broken record is data trouble, not process trouble: every runner catches and logs exceptions per iteration, so one bad payload parks a row without stopping the loop.

items.title: Related components
items.text:
• Academic API Importer — retrieves the large result sets from vendor APIs (Scopus today) and uploads them to blob storage; its "ingest bridge" is intended to feed the search_ingest table so the transfer starts automatically.
  • DESTinY repository — the target index. Interaction is via destiny_sdk: an HMAC-signed RobotClient for polling/submitting enhancement batches and a Keycloak-OAuth OAuthClient for reference lookups and enhancement requests. See Authentication.
  • Monitoring pipeline — scripts/tracking.sql records counters into a monitoring table every minute (via the sql-cron Compose service), scripts/compact.sql aggregates them daily. See Monitoring.

items.title: Configuration
items.text: All configuration is read from environment variables via pydantic-settings (app/util/config.py). Settings are loaded from (in order of increasing precedence) .config/.env.secret, .config/.env, .env.secret, .env, and the actual process environment. Unknown variables are ignored. The canonical list of options is the Settings class — the table below mirrors it.

items.title: Repository & authentication
items.text:
Variable Default Description BASE_URL https://api.staging.evidence-repository.org DESTinY repository API endpoint. ROBOT_ID — (required) Robot client ID (UUID), issued at robot registration. ROBOT_SECRET — (required) Secret for HMAC-signing robot API calls. KEYCLOAK_ID / KEYCLOAK_SECRET — (required at runtime) Keycloak client credentials used for reference lookups and enhancement requests. KEYCLOAK_URL https://auth.evidence-repository.org/ Keycloak server. KEYCLOAK_REALM destiny Keycloak realm. ENV staging Deployment label (local, development, staging, test). Informational — the robot always authenticates. REPOSITORY_PROVENANCE PIK Metadata Cache Provenance/source string attached to submitted enhancements.

Robot identity

ROBOT_NAME and ROBOT_VERSION are derived from pyproject.toml and only need overriding in exceptional cases.

items.title: Database (metadata cache)
items.text:
Variable Default Description DB_HOST localhost Postgres host (postgres inside Docker Compose). DB_PORT 5432 Postgres port. DB_NAME references Database name. DB_USER pguser Database user. DB_PASSWORD password Database password.

Keep DB_NAME consistent

The code default is references, but the postgres service in compose.yaml creates the database from ${DB_NAME:-meta_cache}. Set DB_NAME explicitly in .env so the robot and the container agree.

items.title: Runner pacing & batching
items.text: Variable Default Description MATCH_INTERVAL_SECONDS 30 Sleep between match-loop iterations. ENHANCE_INTERVAL_SECONDS 30 Sleep between enhance-loop iterations. QUEUE_INTERVAL_SECONDS 3600 Sleep between checks for new transfer requests. REQUEST_BATCH_SIZE 10 Records evaluated against the repository per match-loop iteration. FULFIL_BATCH_SIZE 10 References requested per enhancement batch poll. REPOSITORY_LOOKUP_BATCH_SIZE 100 Max identifiers per repository lookup call (1–100; IDs travel in the URL). REPOSITORY_LOOKUP_CONCURRENCY 1 Max concurrent lookup requests.

items.title: Enhancement rules
items.text:
These decide which records the match runner even considers, and how it judges them (see the Enhancement rules page):

Variable Default Description MATCH_IDENTIFIER doi Identifier used to search and match queued records against ODS references: doi or open_alex. Other DESTinY identifier types are not implemented yet, and open_alex matches nothing while transfers leave that column empty (see Matching → How records reach the check). MIN_ABSTRACT_LENGTH 200 Shorter abstracts are never considered (in either direction). MAX_ABSTRACT_LENGTH 10000 Abstracts this long or longer are considered untrustworthy (in either direction): neither submitted nor treated as "already covered". MAX_TITLE_SLOP 10 Max normalised edit distance for titles to count as the same paper. USE_SLOP_FOR_ENHANCEMENT_CHECK false Off: any trustworthy repository abstract counts as "we already have it". On: abstracts are compared and only a similar one counts. MAX_ABSTRACT_SLOP 100 Max normalised edit distance for abstracts to count as identical. Only used when USE_SLOP_FOR_ENHANCEMENT_CHECK is enabled. PUBLICATION_YEAR_TOLERANCE 2 Years are allowed to be this many years apart when both are known.

items.title: Transfer (queue runner)
items.text: Variable Default Description API_WRAPPER_ENDPOINT http://localhost:8000/api Public REST API of the Academic API Importer tool (used for progress reporting). API_WRAPPER_API_KEY very-secret Auth key for that API. API_WRAPPER_CHECKPOINT_INTERVAL 1000 Rows per commit/checkpoint while transferring a file. TRANSFER_LOCKS_PATH .locks Directory holding per-ingest file locks. On a shared host this must be a filesystem all transfer processes can see.

items.title: Logging
items.text:
Logging uses a standard Python dictConfig file, .config/logging.json by default (override with LOG_CONFIG). It silences chatty third-party loggers (sqlalchemy, httpx, azure, …); edit it to raise database or HTTP verbosity when debugging.

The root level is overridden per run by the --loglevel CLI option (defaults to INFO), or by LOGLEVEL when the runner initialises logging without an explicit level.

uv run python run_robot.py match --loglevel DEBUG

items.title: Data model
items.text: The robot owns its Postgres database and treats it as the durable work queue between runners. There are exactly three tables owned by the runners, all created automatically from the SQLModel definitions in app/db/schemas.py at startup (SQLModel.metadata.create_all). The ops scripts additionally maintain a fourth, plain key/value monitoring table (created by scripts/tracking.sql, see Monitoring).

items.title: records — the metadata cache
items.text:
One row per raw source record (one JSONL line from an export file). The record is stored unparsed and only converted into bibliographic fields when a runner needs it — a thin per-format parser (ParsedRecord._parse_record_kwargs) maps the raw payload of a given format (currently scopus_api) onto title, abstract, publication year and identifiers.

Why raw-first storage?

Converting on read keeps the ingestion step trivial and lets converter fixes be applied retroactively without re-fetching source data. The raw JSON also travels to the repository as a RawEnhancement, so nothing is lost. Formats beyond Scopus are explicitly out of scope for now.

items.title: Identifier columns
items.text:
Column Notes record_id Internal primary key (UUIDv6, time-ordered). openalex_id, doi, wos_id, scopus_id, s2_id, pubmed_id, dimensions_id External identifiers (indexed). OpenAlex IDs are normalised to W\d+, DOIs lowercased without URL prefix.

Which DESTinY references a record matched is not a column here — a record can match several references, so those live in m2m_record_ods.

items.title: Payload columns
items.text: Column Notes format Source shape of the raw payload (scopus_api, wos_api, pubmed_api, dimensions_api, openalex_api, pik_solr). raw The untouched source record as JSONB. created_at When the record was queued; also used as the source export date approximation on raw enhancements.

items.title: Tracking columns
items.text:
Every flag is written by a specific step of the pipeline, which makes progress observable and lets each runner pick up exactly where it left off. These three describe the record itself; what the robot did about each reference it matched is tracked per match instead (see m2m_record_ods).

Column Set by Meaning has_eligible_abstract Match runner (batch pick-up) false if the record's own abstract is too short to ever be submitted (MIN_ABSTRACT_LENGTH); such records are skipped from then on. encountered_parsing_error Match runner (batch pick-up) Raw payload could not be parsed, or the parsed record failed validation. Parked until the flag is reset (see below). evaluated Match runner The record has been checked against the repository once.

A record therefore walks a funnel like this (each stage is one indexed column or one row in m2m_record_ods, so every batch query is a simple "where not yet done" filter):

flowchart LR
    NEW["queued<br/><i>(ingest transfer)</i>"] --> PARSE{"raw payload<br/>parses?"}
    PARSE -- "no" --> PARKED["encountered<br/>parsing_error"]
    PARKED -. "parser fixed,<br/>flag reset" .-> ELIG
    PARSE -- yes --> ELIG{"has_eligible<br/>abstract?"}
    ELIG -- "no (too short)" --> DEAD["skipped"]
    ELIG -- yes --> EVAL["evaluated"]
    EVAL -- "no match in ODS" --> NOMATCH["no match row"]
    EVAL -- matched --> MATCHROW["row in<br/>m2m_record_ods"]
    MATCHROW -- "rules reject" --> NOTREQ["enhancement<br/>not required"]
    MATCHROW -- "rules pass" --> REQ["enhancement<br/>requested"]
    REQ --> SUB["enhancement<br/>submitted"]

    style DEAD fill:transparent
    style PARKED fill:#f6e7d7,stroke:#c58b4b

Everything the match stage learns — the record's evaluated flag, the new match rows and their flags — is persisted in a single transaction per batch, so an interrupted run never leaves a half-updated batch behind.

A parked record is not evaluated

A record that fails to parse never reaches the repository, so it never gets evaluated = true. That is why the batch query also excludes encountered_parsing_error = true rows: without that filter the same broken rows would be picked up again on every iteration (and, once enough of them filled a batch, starve the runner of work it could actually do).

items.title: Parser fixes
items.text:
Parsing is deliberately lazy — raw payloads are converted only when a runner needs them, so a parser fix can be applied retroactively to records that were queued before it existed. The error flag is the parking brake that makes that safe: a record whose shape the current parser cannot handle is flagged and set aside instead of aborting the whole batch, the robot keeps working through everything it can parse, and the parked records are picked up again once the parser understands them:

-- What is parked, and what did it fail on?  (the reason is in the match runner's log)
SELECT format, count(*) FROM records WHERE encountered_parsing_error GROUP BY format;

-- After deploying the parser fix: let the runner try again
UPDATE records SET encountered_parsing_error = false WHERE encountered_parsing_error;

No restart is strictly needed — the runner re-reads the table every MATCH_INTERVAL_SECONDS, so clearing the flag is enough for the next loop to pick the records up. Restart the match runner when the parser itself changed, of course.

items.title: m2m_record_ods — the matched references
items.text:
One row per record/reference pair the match runner found. Both directions are genuinely many-to-many: one lookup (say a DOI) can hit several references the repository has not merged yet, and several cached rows from different exports can point at the same reference. The reference itself is not copied here — only its ID, so the pairing survives restarts without duplicating repository data.

The existence of a row is the statement that a reference was found; there is no separate "we found something" flag on records.

erDiagram
    records ||--o{ m2m_record_ods : "matched to"
    ODS_REFERENCE ||--o{ m2m_record_ods : "is matched by"

    records {
        uuid record_id PK "cached raw record"
    }
    ODS_REFERENCE {
        uuid destiny_id PK "in the repository, not in this database"
    }
    m2m_record_ods {
        uuid record_id PK "foreign key to records"
        uuid destiny_id PK "indexed"
        bool abstract_enhancement_required
        bool enhancement_requested
        bool enhancement_submitted
    }
Column Set by Meaning record_id Match runner First half of the composite primary key; foreign key to records with ON DELETE CASCADE. destiny_id Match runner Second half of the primary key; the reference's ID in the repository (indexed — the enhance runner looks up by it). abstract_enhancement_required Match runner The enhancement rules say we should submit this record's abstract for this reference. enhancement_requested Match runner An enhancement request was successfully sent to the repository for this reference (stays false if sending failed). enhancement_submitted Enhance runner The enhancement actually reached the repository for this reference.

Why the flags are not on records

Whether an enhancement is wanted, requested or submitted is a property of the pair: the rules compare one record's abstract against one reference's abstract, the repository grants enhancement per reference, and a record matched to two references may need to enhance only one of them. Keeping the flags on the match row is what makes "we already asked about this reference" observable even when the same record matched several of them.

Two consequences for the runners:

  • Re-evaluating a record does not duplicate matches. persist_match_results inserts only the pairs it does not already know, so a record that is picked up again after a parser fix keeps its history (and its already-requested references).
  • The enhance runner serves one record per reference. When the repository hands out an approved batch of DESTinY IDs, the store joins this table and picks a single cached row per ID — several rows claiming the same reference only need one enhancement.

items.title: search_ingest — transfer requests
items.text:
One row per source file to ingest. This is both the signal to the queue runner ("there is work") and the progress tracker ("resume here if we crash").

Column Notes ingest_id Primary key (UUIDv6, also used as the file-lock name). azure_link SAS URL of the JSONL file in blob storage. Contains credentials — treat as secret. is_queueing A transfer run has claimed this request. is_queued The transfer completed; all rows are in records. checkpoint_bytes Byte offset of the last commit — the resume point after a crash. checkpoint_rows Total number of lines transferred so far.

items.title: Transfer lifecycle
items.text:
stateDiagram-v2
    [*] --> Open: row inserted (via IngestTracker / ingest bridge)
    Open --> Queueing: queue runner takes file lock and marks is_queueing
    Queueing --> Queueing: stream JSONL from checkpoint_bytes, log checkpoints every N rows
    Queueing --> Queued: end of file reached, mark is_queued
    Queued --> [*]
    Queueing --> Queueing: crashed - lock released by OS, next runner resumes from checkpoint

The queue runner always looks at open requests first (is_queueing = false AND is_queued = false), then at partially transferred ones, and only processes a request it can lock exclusively. This makes multiple queue-runner processes safe to run side by side, and makes restarting an interrupted file the normal case rather than an error.

items.title: Prerequisites
items.text:
• uv for dependency and virtual-environment management
  • Docker (for the Compose stack with Postgres)
  • Access to a DESTinY repository deployment — locally or a registered robot on staging/production

items.title: Local setup
items.text:
Install dependencies and activate the environment:

uv sync
source .venv/bin/activate

Create an environment file (.config/.env.example is a starting point — see Configuration for the full list):

cp .config/.env.example .env

At minimum you need ROBOT_ID, ROBOT_SECRET and the Keycloak client credentials. If you run against a local repository deployment that doesn't enforce authentication you can use dummy credentials, but the robot will still try to sign requests, so point it at a deployment that ignores signatures.

items.title: Database
items.text:
For local development, Postgres runs as part of the Docker Compose stack. Tables are not created by SQL scripts — init.sql is a placeholder; the schema is created automatically by SQLModel (SQLModel.metadata.create_all) when a runner starts.

There are no migrations

create_all only creates missing tables — it never changes an existing one. After a schema change in app/db/schemas.py, either drop the volume (docker compose down -v) or apply the CREATE TABLE / ALTER TABLE statements by hand; the robot runs happily against a database that already matches the models.

Useful commands:

docker compose up -d postgres
docker compose logs -f postgres
psql postgresql://pguser:password@127.0.0.1:5432/references   # the port is published to the host
docker compose down    # add -v to drop the database volume

To point the robot at a different database (e.g. the VM below), set DB_HOST in your .env file.

items.title: Running the robot
items.text:
Run a single runner:

uv run python run_robot.py match      # evaluate cached records against the repository
uv run python run_robot.py enhance    # fulfil approved enhancement batches
uv run python run_robot.py queue      # stream export files from blob storage into the cache

Run the whole Compose stack (database, all three runners, plus monitoring helpers):

docker compose up --build

Services in compose.yaml:

Service Runs postgres Postgres 18, volume-persisted, port published to 127.0.0.1:5432 match python run_robot.py match with DB_HOST=postgres enhance python run_robot.py enhance with DB_HOST=postgres queue python run_robot.py queue with DB_HOST=postgres and the shared locks volume mounted at /app/.data/locks locks-init one-shot: creates the host locks directory with the right ownership before queue starts sql-cron runs scripts/tracking.sql every minute and scripts/compact.sql daily (see Monitoring) 
docker compose logs -f match
docker compose logs -f enhance
docker compose logs -f queue
docker compose down

items.title: Feeding data manually
items.text:
A transfer request can be inserted directly:

INSERT INTO search_ingest (azure_link) VALUES ('https://<storage>.blob.core.windows.net/<container>/<file>.jsonl?<SAS-token>');

…or by calling IngestTracker.add_ingest(azure_link=...). Progress can be watched via:

SELECT ingest_id, is_queueing, is_queued, checkpoint_bytes, checkpoint_rows FROM search_ingest;
SELECT r.evaluated, m.destiny_id IS NOT NULL AS matched, m.abstract_enhancement_required,
       m.enhancement_requested, m.enhancement_submitted, count(*)
FROM records r LEFT JOIN m2m_record_ods m ON m.record_id = r.record_id
GROUP BY 1,2,3,4,5 ORDER BY 6 DESC;

items.title: Authentication against the DESTinY repository
items.text:
The robot talks to the repository through two destiny_sdk clients (set up in app/util/repository.py):

  • RobotClient — HMAC-signed calls (request signature with ROBOT_SECRET) for polling enhancement batches and submitting batch results.
  • OAuthClient + Keycloak — client-credentials OAuth for reference lookups and enhancement requests.

To run against a real deployment, register the robot following the ODS robot-registration procedure; registration yields the ROBOT_ID and ROBOT_SECRET. Keycloak client credentials are provisioned separately by the deployment.

items.title: Code quality
items.text:
Before committing, run the pre-commit hooks (formatting, linting, type checks) to keep diffs minimal:

uv run pre-commit install             # once (optional)
uv run pre-commit run --all-files     # manually

Hooks are configured in .pre-commit-config.yaml.

items.title: Documentation
items.text:
The docs site lives in docs/ and is built with Zensical (Material-compatible). Sources are in docs/docs/, configuration in docs/zensical.toml.

uv run zensical serve --config-file docs/zensical.toml  # live preview at http://127.0.0.1:8000
uv run zensical build --config-file docs/zensical.toml --clean

items.title: Operations notes
items.text:
• Restart safety: every runner can be killed and restarted at any time — see Architecture → Crash resilience.
  • Parser fixes: records the parser could not handle are parked with encountered_parsing_error while the robot keeps working; clear the flag to have them retried, see Data model → Parser fixes.
  • Matching key: switch MATCH_IDENTIFIER between doi and open_alex to change which identifier the match runner looks records up by. DOI is the only one the transfer parsers currently fill, so the alternative silently matches nothing until openalex_id is populated.
  • Cleanup: automatic — scripts/compact.sql (via sql-cron) purges submitted or ineligible records older than 14 days, see Monitoring → Compacting.
  • Monitoring: metric collection, compaction and the snapshot query are described on the Monitoring page.
  • Deployment: current deployment runs the Compose stack (or bare processes) on a PIK VM with a hosted Postgres. infra/ contains Azure Container App Terraform scaffolding carried over from the toy-robot template — its variable names predate the current Settings and need updating before use.

items.title: Enhancement rules
items.text:
The heart of the robot is a deliberately simple question, asked once per cached record by the match runner (MatchRunner.should_enhance, app/robots/match.py):

Is this cached abstract sufficiently different (or the repository abstract sufficiently absent/broken) that submitting it improves the index without a meaningful risk of overwriting something correct?

This is not deduplication — it is a plausibility filter. Full deduplication and data fusion will live in the proper ingestion flow that eventually replaces this robot.

items.title: How records reach the check
items.text:
1. The match runner selects the next REQUEST_BATCH_SIZE records whose evaluated flag is not yet true, which were not already ruled out via has_eligible_abstract = false, and which are not parked with encountered_parsing_error.
  2. Each picked row is parsed lazily from its raw payload. A row that cannot be parsed — the per-format parser asserting, or the parsed result failing schema validation — is flagged encountered_parsing_error = true, logged as a warning and left behind. The runner does not stop: the rest of the batch is processed normally, and parked rows are skipped by later batches until the flag is reset (see Data model → Parser fixes).
  3. Records whose own abstract is shorter than MIN_ABSTRACT_LENGTH are flagged has_eligible_abstract = false and dropped — they can never produce a useful enhancement. (The upper length bound is not part of this cheap pre-filter; over-long abstracts are rejected later by the decision tree below.)
  4. The remaining records are looked up in the repository by the identifier configured in MATCH_IDENTIFIER — DOI by default, OpenAlex ID also wired up (app/util/repository.py). Every reference the lookup returns is checked independently — if one identifier maps to more than one canonical reference, each one passes or fails on its own merits.

Which identifier to match on

MATCH_IDENTIFIER takes a DESTinY ExternalIdentifierType value and is mapped in ID_FIELDS onto the cache column to read (DOI → doi, OPEN_ALEX → openalex_id). Only mapped values are accepted: anything else raises NotImplementedError inside the loop, which the runner logs on every iteration while processing no records. A key is only as good as the data behind it, though — the lookup sends only identifiers that are actually present on the parsed record, and rows carrying none are passed over silently (at most the runner's debug log reports a lookup of zero IDs). Transferred rows are inserted with every identifier column empty; it is the format parser that lifts identifiers out of the raw payload, and the Scopus parser currently recovers only the DOI (alongside the Scopus EID). That is why doi is the default: open_alex is wired up identically, but it matches nothing until something populates that column. Both keys are imperfect even when present — see Design rationale for why the plausibility checks exist regardless of the chosen identifier.

items.title: The decision tree
items.text:
flowchart TD
    START(["matched cache record<br/>+ repository reference"]) --> A{"cached abstract exists and<br/>MIN_ABSTRACT_LENGTH ≤ length<br/>< MAX_ABSTRACT_LENGTH?"}
    A -- "no" --> REJ1(["reject<br/><i>missing, too short or<br/>implausibly long abstract</i>"])
    A -- yes --> B{"reference has a DESTinY ID?"}
    B -- "no" --> REJ2(["reject<br/><i>defensive check</i>"])
    B -- yes --> C{"publication year within<br/>PUBLICATION_YEAR_TOLERANCE<br/>of any known year?<br/><i>(skipped if either side unknown)</i>"}
    C -- "no" --> REJ3(["reject<br/><i>probably not the same paper</i>"])
    C -- "yes / unknown" --> D{"normalised title within<br/>MAX_TITLE_SLOP of any<br/>known title?<br/><i>(skipped if either side unknown)</i>"}
    D -- "no" --> REJ4(["reject<br/><i>different paper despite<br/>shared identifier</i>"])
    D -- "yes / unknown" --> E{"repository has a trustworthy<br/>abstract (MIN_ABSTRACT_LENGTH<br/>< length < MAX_ABSTRACT_LENGTH)?"}
    E -- "no" --> OK(["accept —<br/>request enhancement"])
    E -- yes --> F{"USE_SLOP_FOR_ENHANCEMENT_CHECK<br/>enabled and distance ><br/>MAX_ABSTRACT_SLOP?"}
    F -- yes --> OK
    F -- "no" --> REJ5(["reject<br/><i>we already have a<br/>good enough abstract</i>"])

    style REJ1 fill:#f6d7d7,stroke:#b85450
    style REJ2 fill:#f6d7d7,stroke:#b85450
    style REJ3 fill:#f6d7d7,stroke:#b85450
    style REJ4 fill:#f6d7d7,stroke:#b85450
    style REJ5 fill:#f6d7d7,stroke:#b85450
    style OK fill:#d7e8d0,stroke:#5a8a52

items.title: About the comparisons
items.text:
• Titles and abstracts are normalised before comparison: lowercased, all non-a-z characters removed. This catches formatting/encoding noise cheaply while keeping the logic honest about being a heuristic.
  • Year and title checks are skipped whenever either side has no information — absence of data is never treated as a mismatch.
  • Abstract length is used as a trustworthiness signal on both sides: only abstracts between MIN_ABSTRACT_LENGTH and MAX_ABSTRACT_LENGTH count. An over-long repository abstract is treated as broken garbage and does not block an enhancement — and an over-long cached abstract is never submitted.
  • How a trustworthy repository abstract is judged depends on USE_SLOP_FOR_ENHANCEMENT_CHECK:
  • Off (default): mere presence of a trustworthy abstract is enough — "someone already wrote something of plausible quality here, leave it alone". No similarity is computed.
  • On: the abstracts are compared, and only a sufficiently similar repository abstract (distance ≤ MAX_ABSTRACT_SLOP) suppresses the enhancement.
  • The similarity measure (used for titles, and for abstracts in slop mode) is a difflib.ndiff-based per-character distance over the normalised strings, not a semantic check. Tuning the slop thresholds quickly becomes a slippery slope, so the thresholds are intentionally blunt (see MAX_TITLE_SLOP / MAX_ABSTRACT_SLOP in Configuration).

items.title: What gets submitted
items.text:
For every accepted record the enhance runner submits two enhancements (see Repository._records_to_enhancements):

Enhancement Content AbstractContentEnhancement The cached abstract (process = OTHER). RawEnhancement The entire raw source record plus known external identifiers and the source export date — nothing is thrown away, so future pipelines can use fields this robot ignores.

Both are submitted with RESTRICTED visibility and a provenance string built from REPOSITORY_PROVENANCE and the source database, e.g. PIK Metadata Cache (SCOPUS).

Why submit the raw payload even when the abstract is rejected?

It isn't — currently raw enhancements accompany accepted abstracts only. The open question of attaching RawEnhancements to all plausible matches (not just those with a new abstract) was raised in issue #7 and is not implemented.

items.title: Design rationale
items.text:
The rules were refined while planning the API-wrapper ingestion (issue #7, PR #8). Key decisions and accepted trade-offs:

  • Match by identifier only. Whichever identifier MATCH_IDENTIFIER picks, it is not perfectly reliable — production data shows roughly 1 in 500 DOIs held by two unmerged references. The year + title plausibility checks exist precisely so that a wrong identifier match fails the rules instead of getting a wrong abstract. DOI is the default for a mundane reason: it is the identifier the transfer parsers actually recover from raw payloads at the moment, whereas the OpenAlex ID column stays empty (both keys run through the same code, so open_alex starts working as soon as that column is filled).
  • Title similarity was added compared to the first version of the robot (which only checked year tolerance and abstract mismatch) to reduce false-positive matches.
  • "Different enough" replaces "always submit". Rather than offering any abstract we have, we only submit when the repository lacks a trustworthy abstract for the reference — and, in the opt-in similarity mode, lacks a similar one. We deliberately do not try to judge which abstract "looks better" (e.g. always preferring the longer one) — that decision belongs to a future best-abstract mechanism.
  • Presence-only checking is the default. Comparing abstract text cheaply conflates "different wording of the same abstract" with "a genuinely better abstract", and any submission risks burying a good existing one. So the default mode submits only where no plausible abstract exists at all; USE_SLOP_FOR_ENHANCEMENT_CHECK restores the old distance-based comparison for deployments that want to push replacements.
  • Length bounds abstract trustworthiness in both directions. Very short payloads carry no information, and absurdly long ones are usually parsing garbage (affiliation dumps, whole first pages) — so abstracts outside MIN_ABSTRACT_LENGTH … MAX_ABSTRACT_LENGTH neither block enhancements nor get submitted.
  • Double submissions are acceptable. The repository handles duplicate enhancements; the robot does not spend effort preventing them.
  • No new references. The robot only enhances what already exists in the index.

items.title: Monitoring
items.text:
The robot reports through its database — there is no metrics server and nothing is pushed anywhere. A small sql-cron service (in compose.yaml) runs SQL scripts from scripts/ on a schedule: one collects counters into a monitoring table, one keeps that table (and the cache itself) from growing without bound, and one turns the stored counters into a readable snapshot.

flowchart LR
    subgraph cache["Postgres cache"]
        DATA[("records ·<br/>m2m_record_ods ·<br/>search_ingest")]
        MON[("monitoring<br/><i>timestamp · key ·<br/>value · type</i>")]
    end
    TRACK["scripts/tracking.sql<br/><i>sql-cron: every minute</i>"]
    COMPACT["scripts/compact.sql<br/><i>sql-cron: daily at 10:00</i>"]
    VIEW["scripts/monitor.sql<br/><i>run ad hoc</i>"]

    DATA -->|"count funnel flags"| TRACK
    TRACK -->|"append snapshot<br/>(type = orig)"| MON
    MON -->|"read aged-out rows"| COMPACT
    COMPACT -->|"rewrite as daily<br/>min/avg/max, prune"| MON
    COMPACT -->|"purge submitted /<br/>ineligible rows"| DATA
    MON -->|"pivot latest<br/>snapshots"| VIEW

items.title: Collecting — tracking.sql (every minute)
items.text:
The monitoring table is a plain key/value time series (timestamp, key, value, type) created on first run by the script itself — it is the only table not defined by SQLModel. Each run appends one snapshot of counters (as orig rows), so progress is observable as a trend instead of only in the log stream.

Currently tracked metrics:

Transfer state (counted over search_ingest):

Metric Counts ingest_entries transfer requests in total ingest_entries_running transfers claimed (is_queueing) but not finished ingest_entries_finished transfers completed (is_queued) ingest_entries_progress:<ingest_id> final size (checkpoint_rows) of one transfer — one series per request

Record funnel (counted over records — see Data model → Tracking columns):

Metric Counts records_total rows in the cache records_has_eligible_abstract rows whose abstract passed the length pre-filter records_evaluated rows checked against the repository records_encountered_parsing_error rows parked because their raw payload could not be parsed

Match funnel (counted over m2m_record_ods, one row per record/reference pair — see Data model → m2m_record_ods):

Metric Counts matches_total references the cached records were matched to matches_abstract_enhancement_required pairs the enhancement rules accepted matches_enhancement_requested pairs an enhancement request was sent for matches_enhancement_submitted pairs whose enhancement actually reached the repository

Because one record can match several references, the match counters intentionally run ahead of the record counters: matches_total / records_evaluated is roughly how many repository hits an average record gets.

Reading required-but-unrequested pairs

matches_abstract_enhancement_required − matches_enhancement_requested is the number of accepted pairs whose enhancement request has not gone out. A momentary gap is normal queueing; a gap that persists is a failing request API: when the repository is unreachable, the match runner logs it (Enhancement request for … failed) and records the batch anyway, leaving those pairs required without requested. The runner does not retry them by itself — re-request them (or sweep for that flag combination) once the repository answers again, before the 14-day purge takes the rows.

Reading the parsing-error counter

The robot keeps working when it hits an unparsable payload, so this metric is the only thing that surfaces a parser gap: any growth means rows are being parked, and the reason is in the match runner's log (Failed record parsing: … / Failed record validation: …). Fix the parser and clear the flag before the 14-day purge removes those rows — see Data model → Parser fixes.

To add a metric, append an INSERT INTO monitoring SELECT now(), '<key>', count(...), 'orig' FROM ... statement to tracking.sql — and add a matching CASE WHEN column to monitor.sql, whose pivot columns are hardcoded.

items.title: Compacting — compact.sql (daily at 10:00)
items.text:
Three housekeeping passes in one script:

  1. Aggregate aged-out metrics. Raw (orig) rows older than seven days are collapsed into one daily min / avg / max row per metric key, and the raw rows are dropped.
  2. Cap the table size. Only the 10,000 most recent monitoring rows survive each run.
  3. Purge cache rows that no longer matter. Records older than 14 days that are not parked and have no match still awaiting its enhancement (required and not yet submitted) are deleted from records; their m2m_record_ods rows follow via ON DELETE CASCADE. The cache therefore does not grow forever while the raw source data stays in (cold) blob storage anyway and can be re-ingested via a new search_ingest row.

The purge can outrun the match runner

A record without match rows counts as settled — so records that were never evaluated (e.g. the robot was down while a large transfer ran) are also deleted once they are 14 days old, and will never be retried. Lengthen the interval if your batches may lag that far behind.

items.title: Viewing — monitor.sql (ad hoc)
items.text:
monitor.sql pivots the newest monitoring snapshots into a wide table — one row per minute, one column per metric, newest first (last 500 rows):

psql postgresql://pguser:password@127.0.0.1:5432/references -f scripts/monitor.sql

Optional Evidence dashboard

An OpenTelemetry setup exists in the Docker image (opentelemetry-* deps) but is not configured end to end.
